1. This appeal is filed by the claimant, being dissatisfied with the quantum of compensation and award dated 06.11.2020 passed in M.V.C.No.611/2017 by the learned Senior Civil Judge and MACT VI, at Kudligi, sitting at Sandur (hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal').
2. Brief facts, leading rise to the filing of this appeal are as follows:
On 22.12.2016, the petitioner met with an accident and sustained grievous injuries.
The accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The petitioner thereafter filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the MV Act seeking compensation on account of injuries sustained in the road traffic accident.
Accordingly, prays to allow the claim petition.

3. The respondent-NEKSRTC filed a statement of objections denying the averments made in the claim petition and contented that the accident was not caused due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending bus.
It is contended that the driver was driving the bus cautiously and on NC: 2026:KHC-D:3578 HC-KAR the proper side of the road.
Accordingly, the respondent NEKSRTC prayed for dismissal of the claim petition against it.
4. A Notice was issued to the driver.
Despite the service of notice, the driver remained unrepresented and the Tribunal placed him ex-parte.
The other passengers of the bus also filed a claim petitions.
The Tribunal clubbed all the claim petitions, and framed the separate issues.
5. The petitioner in the instant case was examined as PW-1, also examined the Doctor as PW-4, and marked 39 documents as Ex.P1 to P39.

The respondent-driver was examined as RW-1.
6.

The Tribunal, after assessing the verbal and documentary evidence, allowed the claim petition in part with costs vide judgment dated 06.11.2020 and awarded a compensation of 2,43,386/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the petition till its realisation.

sentences.text: The petitioner, being dissatisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, has preferred the present appeal seeking enhancement of the compensation.

8. Heard the argument of the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned counsel for the NEKSRTC.
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3578 HC-KAR 9.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on a lower side.
It is submitted that the petitioner has suffered a permanent disability, and the Tribunal could have awarded a higher compensation under the heads of pain and suffering, and amenities.
The Tribunal awarded a compensation under the heads of pain and suffering 25,000/- and amenities 25,000/- which is on the lower side.
Hence, on these grounds, he prays to enhance the compensation, by allowing the appeal.
10. Per contra, learned counsel for the NEKSRTC submits that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper and do not call for interference at the hands of this Court.
Hence, prays to dismiss the appeal.

11. Perused the records, and considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the parties.
12.
The point that would arise for consideration is regarding the quantum of compensation.

13. It is an undisputed fact that the petitioner met with an accident, and sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident, and the charge sheet was filed against the driver of the KSRTC bus.

The Tribunal, placing reliance on the charge sheet NC: 2026:KHC-D:3578 HC-KAR marked as Ex.P4 has rightly recorded the finding that the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the NEKSRTC bus.
Regarding quantum of compensation 14.
Insofar as the quantum of compensation is concerned, the petitioner, to prove that he has suffered permanent disability, produced the wound certificate marked as Ex.P6.
It is also noted that even after accident, the petitioner is continued in the service.
During the course of cross-examination of PW-1, he admitted that still he is working in the NMDC.
Accordingly, the Tribunal has rightly declined to award the compensation under the head of loss of future income.
15. Considering the medical records, this Court is of the opinion that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on a lower side.
The petitioner, is therefore, entitled to a global compensation of 3,50,000/- including the compensation awarded by the Tribunal.

16. Thus, in view of the above discussion, I proceed to pass the following:
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3578 HC-KAR ORDER

sentences.text: 3 (i) The appeal is allowed-in-part.
(ii) The judgment and award dated 06.11.2020 passed in M.V.C.No.611/2017 by the Tribunal is hereby modified.

(iii) The petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of 3,50,000/- including the compensation awarded by the tribunal along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing of the petition till realisation of the amount.
(iv) The NEKSRTC is directed to deposit the compensation amount along with accrued interest within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
(v) The Tribunal records, and the amount in deposit, if any, shall be transmitted to the Tribunal concerned, forthwith.
